note: Iowa DNR state park on Blue Lake, a 250-acre Missouri River oxbow near Onawa, where Lewis and Clark camped in August 1804; full-size keelboat replica on display. The campground lines the lake's north and east shore, with a swim beach, boat ramps and a 1930s WPA lodge nearby. No daily Iowa park-entry fee, camping fee only. --Claude
summary: Sites -> 76 (+2 youth), max 90, pull-throughs; hookups confirmed; flush toilets added; fcfs some_sites -> never (100% reservable), booking season Apr 1-Oct 31. Waterfront lead down lakefront -> lakeview. Phone to add. Pin within ~100 m.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD DOWN, lakefront -> lakeview. ReserveAmerica tags every one of its 78 sites 'Near Water - no'. Plotting RA's per-site GIS points on imagery puts all 76 numbered sites on the inner loops: the east rows (sites 1-19) sit ~60-80 m from Blue Lake with a sandy shoreline track running between them and the water across an open grass slope, and sites 48-77 sit behind a tree belt 40-60 m further inland. The lake is in open view from the east rows, which supports lakeview. A separate row of ~25-30 back-in pads directly along the north shore (42.0490-42.0498, -96.1668 to -96.1620), pad tails ~20-40 m from the water, has NO RA site on it and is not marked on the DNR map; the shoreline track also runs between those pads and the water. If that row is bookable (newer than RA's GIS data?) it holds the only on-water candidates, but the track between may block it under the 2026-11-01 ruling. Unconfirmed, so down. (Distances are imagery estimates; Overpass/Nominatim were down.)
PHONE: stored phone is empty; the DNR brochure and park page give 'Park Office: 712-423-2829'. apply.py does not write phone.
